sentences.text: It is submitted that the parties have amicably settled their differences and that the Respondent has filed no objection affidavit dated 03.06.2025 to support the quashing of the present FIR.
5. Both the parties are present in person and are identified by the Counsel and the Investigating Officer.
The parties in person submits that they were in a relationship since 2021.

On one day,
because of certain differences, the Complainant in her anger went and made a complaint for which the FIR has been registered.

6. All their differences have been sorted out and submit that they have voluntarily without any fear,
force or coercion, filed present Petition for quashing of the FIR.

7. Submissions heard and record perused.
8.
As per the FIR, the parties were in a relationship since 2021.
In 2023, they contracted HIV but continued to live in the relationship.
Off and on, they kept getting in and out of the relationship on account of the differences.
There are some allegations made that the Petitioner was also involved with another woman.
Eventually, the Complainant decided to live separately in February, 2025 despite which, the Petitioner kept on having relationship with her and assuring her that he would marry her.
Eventually, on 06.05.2025, they had some altercation, which resulted in registration of FIR.

9. Considering that both the are adults and had got into a consensual relationship and have now decided to settle all their disputes amicable, the FIR No. 0209/2025 under Sections 376/269 IPC registered at P.S. Sunlight Colony and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/07/2025 at 21:57:24 10.
The Petition alongwith pending Application, is disposed of accordingly.
NEENA BANSAL KRISHNA, J JULY 9, 2025 N
